intro: ERS–WVSU connects disciplinary expertise with economic reasoning, applied data analysis, and causal inference. We help researchers develop stronger projects—from research questions and evidence to collaborative proposals and policy relevance.
section_one_intro: Researchers in agriculture, business, education, health, environmental science and beyond can strengthen their work through economic framing, rigorous data analysis, causal inference, and transparent interpretation. ERS–WVSU provides a practical setting for that exchange.
pillar_one_text: Clarify incentives, behavior, constraints, trade-offs, and the economic mechanisms behind a research question.
pillar_two_text: Discuss data, econometric specifications, identification strategies, uncertainty, and causal interpretation.
pillar_three_text: Explore joint research designs, stronger papers, policy analysis, and interdisciplinary grant concepts.
regional_text: Researchers from any discipline are welcome when their work offers a meaningful opportunity for economics, data analysis, or causal inference to add value. We are not a general-purpose speaker series; the aim is substantive feedback and potential collaboration.
closing_text: Bring an early idea, a working paper, or an empirical challenge. Presenters do not need to have an economics component already developed. Together we can explore whether—and how—it would strengthen the work.
